item.title: Azerbaijan Promises More Gas to Europe as Production Reality Lags
item.description: The Azerbaijani state energy company SOCAR has announced it is selling natural gas to Austria and Germany. But it remains an open question whether Baku can hit its promised target of delivering 20 billion cubic meters (bcm) of gas to the European Union in the near future. item.description: US naphtha has begun arriving in Venezuelan waters, marking an early and telling step in efforts to restart the country’s long-crippled heavy oil production. item.title: Scientists Pioneer Reverse Solar Panels to Create Energy at Night
item.description: On a global level, solar energy has grown exponentially over the last few decades as costs have plummeted and demand has risen accordingly. item.title: Mexico Weighs Cuba Oil Cut as Trump Pressure Mounts
item.description: Mexico is weighing whether to halt or scale back oil shipments to Cuba as concerns grow within President Claudia Sheinbaum’s government that continuing the policy could trigger retaliation from the United States, according to sources familiar with internal discussions. The review comes at a sensitive moment. item.description: The Trump Administration continues to revise, restructure, and cancel billions of U.S. dollars of Biden-era loans and funding commitments to clean energy projects as the United States shifted its policy to supporting fossil fuels and nuclear power as part of its energy dominance agenda. item.title: Global Energy Transition Threatened by Critical Transformer Shortages
item.description: The global clean energy transition has passed a tipping point as renewable energies have simply become too cheap to fail. item.title: Gold Breaks the $5,000 Barrier as Global Uncertainty Fuels Historic Rally
item.description: Gold prices continued to rally in early Asian trading on Monday, with bullion breaking through the $5,000 per troy ounce threshold for the first time in history. At the time of writing, the price of gold had reached $5,078.70 per ounce, driven by heightened geopolitical tensions and growing investor demand for safe-haven assets amid fiscal concerns in major economies.
